summary.short: Texas SB 6 (2025) amends the Utilities Code and Water Code on electric service to large loads, mainly in the ERCOT power region. It covers interconnection standards, cost and financial commitment rules, disclosure, curtailment, and water-corporation power generation, effective immediately or September 1, 2025.
summary.long: Texas SB 6 amends the Utilities Code and Water Code on electric service for large loads. It directs the Public Utility Commission (PUC) to set interconnection standards for new or expanded loads above a demand threshold, set by default at 75 megawatts in the ERCOT power region. The standards cover disclosure of competing requests, a flat study fee of at least $100,000, site control, uniform financial commitments with conditional refunds, and cost contribution by large load customers. Large loads with on-site backup generation that can serve at least 50 percent of on-site demand must disclose it, and ERCOT may direct them to deploy it or curtail load. Power generation companies must notify ERCOT before netting an existing stand-alone generation resource with a new large load; the PUC may approve, deny or condition such arrangements after an ERCOT study. Loads interconnected after December 31, 2025 must have curtailment protocols, and ERCOT must procure demand reductions from large loads of at least 75 megawatts. Water or sewer corporations may generate power for their own water uses and, if they meet conditions and register, sell excess power. The PUC must evaluate transmission cost allocation and amend rules by December 31, 2026. The Act takes effect immediately if passed by two-thirds of each house, otherwise on September 1, 2025.

enforcement.note: The enacted text of SB 6 contains no penalties, fines, criminal sanctions, license revocations, benefit clawbacks, suspensions or blocking provisions. It sets duties (e.g., Sec. 37.0561, Sec. 39.169, Sec. 39.170) and directs the PUC to adopt rules, but it does not state consequences for non-compliance and does not cite another act's penalty provisions.
